name: Reaction Button
description: Like / favourite / upvote with a count. The icon pops, a ring and a burst of particles fly out in the tone colour, and the count rolls digit by digit. aria-pressed reflects the state.
intents: heart animation when liking a post
usage: Use on posts, comments, products and saved items. Keep the count visible; the burst only plays when turning it on, not off. When the reacted state lives in your data, control it: pass `checked` and `count` and update both in `onChange(checked, count)` (the count it suggests is yours ± 1; send the request there and roll back if it fails). Otherwise seed it with `defaultChecked` and `defaultCount` and listen to `onChange`. Give it a `label` that names the thing ("Like Dune"), since that is its accessible name.

dataProps.description: Controlled reacted state. Pass it with onChange; leave it undefined to let the button keep its own.
Reacted state on first render when uncontrolled.
Old name for defaultChecked (it only seeds the state). Still works; prefer checked or defaultChecked.
Controlled count. Pass it with onChange and update it there; leave it undefined to let the button count on its own from defaultCount.
Count on first render when uncontrolled; each toggle adds or removes one.
(checked: boolean, count: number) => void, on each toggle. count is the current count plus or minus one (never below 0). Not called while disabled.
Accessible name, read with the count ("Like, 12 reactions"). Name the thing: "Like Dune".
Show the rolling count. Off gives an icon-only toggle named by label.
(n: number) => string for the shown and announced count. Default: the number in the Theme's locale.
A built-in icon name (filled when on) or your own node.

Other attributes (aria-*, data-*, id, onClick) go to the <button>; className and style too. An onClick that calls preventDefault() stops the toggle.
